title: Grade 9 Science — Gravitation & Matter in Our Surroundings
description: Gravitation and Matter in Our Surroundings practice questions
subject: science

questions.question: The value of acceleration due to gravity (g) on the surface of the Earth is approximately:
options: Both B and C (9.8 or 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: g ≈ 9.8 m/s² is the precise value. In calculations, g = 10 m/s² is commonly used for simplicity. 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ is the universal gravitational constant G, not g.

questions.question: The weight of an object on the Moon compared to Earth is:
questions.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is about 1/6th of Earth's g. Weight = mg, so weight on Moon = (1/6) × weight on Earth.

questions.question: The weight of a 10 kg object on Earth (g = 10 m/s²) is:
questions.explanation: Weight W = mg = 10 kg × 10 m/s² = 100 N. Weight is a force and is measured in Newtons.

questions.question: According to the universal law of gravitation, force between two masses is:
options: Proportional to the sum of masses
Inversely proportional to the product of masses
Proportional to the product of masses and inversely proportional to the square of distance
questions.explanation: F = Gm₁m₂/r². Force is directly proportional to the product of the two masses (m₁m₂) and inversely proportional to the square of the distance (r²) between them.

questions.question: Kepler's second law (law of areas) states that a planet sweeps equal areas in equal times. This implies that a planet moves:
options: Fastest when farthest from the Sun
At constant speed throughout its orbit
Fastest when closest to the Sun
questions.explanation: To sweep equal areas in equal times, a planet must move faster when closer to the Sun (where the radius is short) and slower when farther away.

questions.question: Archimedes' principle states that when an object is immersed in a fluid, it experiences a buoyant force equal to:
options: The weight of the fluid displaced
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle: the buoyant force (upthrust) on an object equals the weight of fluid displaced by the object. This explains why objects float or sink.

questions.question: An object thrown horizontally from a height falls under gravity. Its horizontal velocity:
options: Becomes zero at the highest point
questions.explanation: In projectile motion, gravity acts only vertically. The horizontal velocity has no horizontal force acting on it (ignoring air resistance), so it remains constant throughout.

questions.question: The mass of an object at the centre of the Earth will be:
questions.explanation: Mass is an intrinsic property of matter — it does not change with location. Weight (= mg) changes because g changes, but mass remains constant everywhere.

questions.question: The state of matter with a definite shape and definite volume is:
questions.explanation: Solids have a fixed shape and fixed volume because their particles are tightly packed and held in fixed positions by strong intermolecular forces.

questions.question: The process by which a solid converts directly to a gas (without passing through the liquid state) is called:
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct conversion of a solid to a gas. Examples: dry ice (CO₂), camphor, iodine, and naphthalene (mothballs) undergo sublimation.

questions.question: Evaporation causes cooling because:
options: High-energy particles escape, taking heat energy with them and cooling the surface
Evaporation absorbs cold from the surroundings
questions.explanation: During evaporation, the most energetic molecules escape from the liquid surface. This loss of high-energy particles lowers the average kinetic energy of the remaining liquid, causing cooling.

questions.question: The boiling point of water at standard atmospheric pressure is:
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100°C (373 K) at standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm). This is when the vapour pressure of water equals atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: Gases exert pressure on the walls of the container because:
options: Gas particles collide with the walls continuously
questions.explanation: Gas particles move rapidly and randomly in all directions. They continuously collide with the walls of the container, and these collisions exert force on the walls — this is gas pressure.

questions.question: The SI unit of temperature is:
questions.explanation: The SI unit of temperature is Kelvin (K). The Kelvin scale starts at absolute zero (0 K = −273.15°C). Celsius is widely used but is not the SI unit.

questions.question: At high altitude (mountain tops), water boils at a temperature:
questions.explanation: At high altitudes, atmospheric pressure is lower. Water boils when vapour pressure equals atmospheric pressure. At lower pressure, this occurs at a lower temperature — below 100°C.
